Thread of three messages, closed this morning. The exchange opened with a general question about how the ASM landscape has shifted over the past few years, kept at a high level with no efficacy claims made on either side, and then moved to the older patients who make up much of this panel. Recap: geriatric patients on multiple medications remain the main barrier; requests interaction education for staff. Two points were stated precisely: (1) most of these pts arrive with medication lists already managed by two or three other prescribers, and (2) the practice has no reference sheet the nursing staff can use during intake. I confirmed the approved adult indication for XCOPRI, noted that I cannot advise on individual regimens, and offered to check what label-level interaction material exists. No dosing figures were exchanged and no off-label question was raised.
Next step: submit an interaction-education request to medical information and reply in writing by January 16.

E02.1:
What started as two lines about last week's storms and a delayed flight home turned into a genuine question, so I am logging the thread rather than leaving it in my inbox. After the pleasantries, the physician asked whether anything has been published in younger patients, explaining that the question tends to surface at the front desk when families of teenaged pts want to know what the plan looks like over the next few years. I said only that cenobamate is approved in the US for adults with focal onset seizures, that I would not speculate beyond that, and that I would check the published record properly before answering. Action item from the email: send any available adolescent safety data or confirm that none exists yet. Neither of us raised off-label use, and no dosing was discussed at any point in the exchange.
Next step: open a medical information request and reply with citations or with a clear statement that none exist.

E03.1:
Thread of three messages dated June 29, June 30 and July 1, logged here as a single recap. The first message was a neutral question about how the ASM landscape has changed since 2020, with no efficacy claims made either way. The second and third went further. Summary of the point raised: repeated adolescent (12-17) drug-resistant cases, nothing to offer on label, families asking why age expansion data does not exist yet. Four such referrals were counted at this center since April, each one having already failed two or more ASMs before the first appt. My reply restated the approved adult indication for cenobamate in the US, declined to comment beyond the label, and confirmed that the observation would be recorded internally as field feedback. No dosing was discussed, and no off-label course of action was proposed or implied at any point.
Next step: record the pattern as a recurring field insight and acknowledge the thread by July 8.
